issues.legal_issue: The appropriate deduction for development expenses must reflect the characteristics of the acquired land and the comparable sale evidence.
material_facts: About 101 acres of land were acquired, and the acquired land was not fully developed.
The landowners relied on a sale of a small parcel of 19 guntas; it had two-road access and was developed, features absent from the acquired land.
The landowners produced no comparable sales of large parcels sold by the acre.
The Reference Court deducted 50% for development expenses. The High Court reduced the deduction to 25% without giving a sufficient reason for doing so.
The market value found by the Reference Court and upheld by the High Court was not challenged before the Supreme Court.
issues.conclusion: The Reference Court was justified in deducting 50% for development expenses. The High Court's reduction to 25% was set aside, and the Reference Court's award was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 23 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, market value is assessed on the relevant statutory parameters. Chimanlal Hargovinddas v. Special Land Acquisition Officer, Poona & Anr. (1988) 3 SCC 751 sets out that comparable sale prices must be adjusted for relevant plus and minus factors, including the size and development of the land, using a common-sense assessment rather than a rigid rule. Union of India v. Raj Kumar Baghal Singh (Dead) Through Legal Representatives & Ors. (2014) 10 SCC 422 reiterates those principles. Trishala Jain & Anr. v. State of Uttaranchal & Anr. (2011) 6 SCC 47 and Vithal Rao & Anr. v. Special Land Acquisition Officer (2017) 8 SCC 558 support making a fact-dependent deduction for development expenses, including when small-parcel sales are used to value a large tract, and using reasonable guesswork where appropriate. The deduction depends on the nature and area of the land, its state of development, and the purpose of acquisition.

rule.if: land_acquisition_compensation_appeal and large_acquired_tract and acquired_land_not_fully_developed and no_comparable_large_parcel_sales and benchmark_is_small_parcel and benchmark_has_advantages_absent_from_acquired_land and appellate_reduction_unreasoned

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning compensation for land acquired for a public purpose.
predicates.large_acquired_tract: The acquiring authority acquired a large tract of land.
predicates.acquired_land_not_fully_developed: The acquired land was not fully developed.
predicates.no_comparable_large_parcel_sales: The parties seeking compensation did not produce comparable sales of large parcels.
predicates.benchmark_is_small_parcel: The sale used as the valuation benchmark concerned a small parcel of land.
predicates.benchmark_has_advantages_absent_from_acq: The benchmark parcel was developed and had road-access advantages that the acquired land did not have.
predicates.appellate_reduction_unreasoned: The appellate court reduced the development deduction made by the lower court without giving a sufficient reason for the reduction.

issues.definition: When a compensation appeal concerns a large, not fully developed tract, no comparable large-parcel sales are available, the small benchmark parcel has advantages absent from the acquired land, and the appellate reduction is unexplained, the lower court's development deduction is restored.
